scenarios.seedOffsetHint: Seconds of seed-derived head start. At zero, every seed replays identical traffic and a multi-seed benchmark reports a variance of zero that is an artefact, not a finding.
scenarios.zeroOffsetWarning: A moving obstacle has zero seed spread: every seed will replay the same traffic, so running more seeds adds episodes but no new evidence.
scenarios.previewHint: Obstacle positions come from the backend at this instant and this seed — the same motion the simulator runs. Traffic timing varies with the seed, so this is one episode, not all of them.
scenarios.notValidatedYet: Not validated yet. Validation runs the real engine, so it is the same check that runs on save.

robot.title: Robot profiles
robot.subtitle: The robot a model was trained for. Change robots with a form, not a code edit.
models.trainingNote: PlanBench currently evaluates PPO models you have already trained. Training here is being built; until it exists there is no button for it.
leaderboard.observationHint: What the controller was allowed to see. Stacks shown different things are solving different problems and are ranked separately.
leaderboard.observationUnknownHint: This result was stored before stacks declared what they see. It is not assumed to match the others.
leaderboard.groupGlobalObservationReplan: Global planner observation: {observation} — replanning was on, so the global planner read the true positions of the moving obstacles. These rows are not comparable with runs that did not replan.
leaderboard.observationGroupingHint: On: only stacks shown the same data are ranked together. Off: they are ranked together anyway, with a warning.
leaderboard.mixedObservationWarning: These rows were not shown the same data. A stack with more information solves an easier problem, so this order is not evidence that one algorithm is better.
algorithms.observationHint: Declared by the registry (P02). Benchmarks compare stacks that were shown the same data; the leaderboard keeps different declarations apart.
detail.medianHint: Travel time, efficiency and smoothness are medians over successful episodes — one episode that stalled until the timeout would drag a mean past anything that happened. Hover a cell for its interquartile range and 95% confidence interval.
detail.statisticsHint: Wilcoxon signed-rank on episodes paired by seed: each pair is the same obstacle motion faced by both stacks. Seeds where either stack failed have no travel time and drop out.
detail.effectSizeHint: Cliff's delta of A against B, in [-1, 1]. Negative means A's values are lower. A p-value says whether a difference could be chance; this says how large it is.
detail.fewSeedsWarning: This benchmark ran {seeds} seeds. That is enough to compute the numbers below and not enough to conclude from them — treat any difference as worth investigating, not as established.
detail.noStrongClaim: Read as: under these conditions and this seed set, one stack scored higher than the other. Whether that difference is real depends on the p-value, the effect size and the seed count together — no single number here settles it.
protocol.splitHint: Dev scenarios are the ones stacks are developed and tuned against. Held-out scenarios are kept aside so a result on them says something about generalization rather than about tuning. The split is protocol metadata: changing it never changes a scenario or the checksum of any benchmark already run on it.
protocol.unassignedHint: Nobody has classified this scenario, so results on it support no claim either way. Scenarios created in the app start here and move only through a reviewed protocol change.
protocol.holdoutWarning: {scenario} is a held-out scenario. It is meant for a final check, not for iterating: every look at it makes the next result on it a little less independent of what you learned from the last one. Running it is recorded.
protocol.holdoutBenchmarkNotice: This benchmark ran on a held-out scenario. Read it as a generalization check; do not tune against it.
protocol.unassignedBenchmarkNotice: This scenario is not assigned to a split, so this result is excluded from the generalization gap.
generalization.title: Generalization gap
generalization.hint: Dev results minus held-out results, per stack, across accepted benchmarks. Each report counts under the split it recorded when it ran, and scenarios are weighted equally. A gap needs both sides: with only one, there is nothing to conclude.
generalization.holdoutUsageHint: Every benchmark that ran a held-out scenario. A held-out set stops being held out by being consulted; this is the count nobody can quietly forget.
charts.difficultyCurveHint: Difficulty is measured (P03), not assumed: it is what fraction of runs the pinned baseline failed. A stack that holds up as the scenarios get harder is a different result from one with the same average that collapses at the right-hand end.
charts.noCalibration: No difficulty calibration has been run, so there is no measured axis to plot against. Run scripts/calibrate_difficulty.py; the curriculum order is a hand-written intention and is deliberately not used as a substitute.
charts.noCurveData: No accepted result sits on a calibrated scenario yet.
charts.uncalibratedScenarios: Not on the curve — no measured difficulty: {scenarios}
charts.staleScenarios: Difficulty measured before the scenario was last edited: {scenarios}
charts.staleDifficulty: The scenario changed after this difficulty was measured.
charts.distributionsHint: The bar is the median. The wide whisker is the interquartile range — how much the runs varied. The narrow whisker is the 95% interval for the median itself — how well this many seeds pin it down. They answer different questions, and a tight interval around a widely varying quantity is not a consistent algorithm.
charts.noDistribution: No distribution to draw — no successful episode: {algorithms}
charts.incompleteGap: Missing one side, so no gap can be computed: {algorithms}
charts.exportHint: The whole report as Markdown: provenance, conditions, observation classes, medians with their intervals, the paired tests and every run. Written so it can be read outside the platform, by somebody without an account.
replanning.hint: Let the robot ask for a new global path when it gets blocked. Off by default: a replan is computed from the true positions of the moving obstacles, so a run with it on is not comparable with one without.
replanning.slowWarning: The robot must stand still for the whole stuck window before it is granted a new path, so the run takes noticeably longer. That wait is simulated time, not the app freezing.
replanning.benchmarkScope: This rule applies to every stack in the sweep — it is a benchmark condition, not an algorithm parameter.
decisions.title: Decisions
decisions.subtitle: Every run, ranked or not. A gate table is a result, not a failure.
decisions.filter.note: Most runs produce no Decision Card. That is the expected outcome when fewer than two candidates clear all six gates, and the gate table is then the whole result.
decisions.episodes.partial: Measured of requested. An interrupted run is a valid smaller comparison.
decisions.empty.title: No selection runs yet
decisions.empty.body: Run a comparison with scripts/compare.py or POST /decisions, and it will appear here whether or not it ranks.
decisions.sample.interrupted: This run was stopped before it finished. What it measured is valid and smaller — every candidate covers the same episodes — but it is not the run that was asked for.
decisions.sample.belowNMin: Fewer episodes than N_min for the declared collision risk (HĐ-7.1). Gate verdicts below rest on a sample smaller than the deployment requires.
decisions.sample.belowNMinInterrupted: Stopped early at {n} of the {min} episodes N_min requires for the declared collision risk (HĐ-7.1). Both facts at once: the run was cut short, and what it did measure is too small to bound the risk the deployment asked for. Every gate verdict and every figure below rests on that sample.
decisions.gates.note: Six feasibility gates run before anything is scored (HĐ-7). A candidate that failed one was never ranked — it is not a worse choice, it is not a choice.
decisions.gates.distinctNote: Distinct episodes, not runs. A hundred replays of one episode is one independent sample.
decisions.noCard.title: No recommendation from this run
decisions.noCard.whatNext.interrupted: What to do: run the remaining episodes. The measurements already on disk are reused.
decisions.noCard.whatNext.gate_only: What to do: rank on a deployment whose threshold leaves room above it. No candidate will change this one — the scale itself has collapsed. Loosening this deployment's threshold to get a card is the move the contract forbids.
decisions.noCard.whatNext.no_survivors: What to do: register a better candidate. Never a softer deployment — the gate table already answered who was eliminated where.
decisions.card.title: Decision Card
decisions.card.sensitivity: Would this recommendation survive being wrong?
decisions.card.scopeNote: This recommendation is scoped to {scope} on this deployment alone (HĐ-1.4). It says nothing about any other map, mission or robot.
decisions.conditions.title: The world this was measured in
decisions.provenance.title: Rebuilding this
decisions.audit.title: Who acted on this
decisions.audit.empty: Nobody has read or approved this run yet.
decisions.acts.title: Read it, and decide on it
decisions.acts.signedOut: Sign in to record that you read this run, or to approve its recommendation.
decisions.acts.commentHint: Optional — what you concluded, for whoever reads this next
decisions.acts.reviewNote: Applies to every run, including the ones that recommend nobody.
decisions.acts.configNote: Approving exports a configuration file. The system is simulation-only — there is no path from here to a robot (HĐ-14).
decisions.acts.whyNoConfig: This run recommends nobody, so there is nothing to approve. Reading it is still worth recording.
decisions.acts.whyDecided: Already {state} by {who}. That decision stands — the way to change a recommendation is a new run, which leaves both records in place.
decisions.acts.whyOwnRun: You started this run, so you cannot approve its recommendation (HĐ-14). Whoever chose the candidates and the deployment is not an independent check on the answer.
deployments.title: Deployments
deployments.subtitle: The question a selection answers: one map, one mission, one robot, declared noise, six thresholds.
deployments.nMinNote: Episodes required by the declared risk (HĐ-7.1). The arrow runs one way: risk decides the count, never the other way round.
deployments.noiseUndeclared: This profile has no sensor_noise block, so it was measured with no noise at all — not with noise somebody set to zero.
deployments.noiseNote: Noise belongs to the deployment, not to a run. Changing it changes the world: episode_context_id does not hash the amplitudes (HĐ-3.1), so a changed deployment needs a new id — and the server refuses to redefine an existing one.
deployments.empty.title: No deployments filed yet
deployments.empty.body: Paste a profile below, or copy one from the profiles/ directory in the repository.
deployments.file.title: File a deployment
deployments.file.signedOut: Sign in to file a deployment.
deployments.file.note: Paste the profile YAML. The server validates it against HĐ-2 — a heading requirement it cannot evaluate, traffic that shifts by less than one period, or a RAM budget that does not add up are all refused with a reason.
deployments.file.placeholder:
id: warehouse_a_v3
claim_level: mission
environment:
  map: maps/warehouse_a.pgm
  ...
deployments.file.idRule: Re-filing the same id with different content is refused, not merged.
decisions.launch.title: Run a comparison
decisions.launch.note: Queued, not run inside this request. Leaving the episode count blank uses N_min from the deployment's declared collision risk (HĐ-7.1) — on a warehouse at 1% that is 300 episodes and hours of simulation.
decisions.launch.oneAtATime: A sweep is running. Only one at a time: two evaluation runs on one machine pin the same cores and each becomes the other's background load, so G4 would measure a machine that does not exist (HĐ-7.4).
trace.title: Watch an episode
trace.note: One Parquet trace per (candidate, episode) is the only input the metrics come from (HĐ-5). Every number in the gate table above was computed from files like this one.
trace.colourNote: The path is coloured by clearance measured from the robot's surface (HĐ-8.2): red at the collision boundary, blue at a full robot radius of room. Red dots are HĐ-5 events — a collision and an arrival draw the same curve, and only the marker tells them apart. Amber circles are the deployment's moving obstacles at that instant, drawn to their declared radius. The dashed line is the route the global planner had asked for at that instant, and it changes colour at every replan — a plan that bent and a plan that was thrown away and redrawn look the same otherwise.
decisions.episodes.notRunNote: This candidate was retired before this episode, so it was never driven — which is not the same as driven and passed, and it is why this candidate's denominator is smaller than the table's.
decisions.episodes.notRecorded: This run was stored before per-episode outcomes were recorded. Its gate table and success rates are unaffected — what is missing is which episodes failed, not whether they did. A new comparison on the same deployment records them.
decisions.episodes.cellNote: min clearance {clearance} m · travel {time} s · p99 latency {latency} ms. Click to open this episode below.
decisions.episodes.noFailures: Every candidate passed every episode in this run.
decisions.launch.submitDerived: File the deployment and queue it
decisions.map.label: Map
decisions.map.pickDeploymentFirst: Choose a deployment first — a custom map is filed as a copy of one, and its robot radius and goal tolerance are what the preview draws to scale.
decisions.map.noMapsYet: No maps stored yet. Draw one first; this list is the map store, not the files on disk.
deployments.mode.note: Both file the same document. Switching to YAML carries what the form built; switching back does not carry it home, so a block the form cannot express would be lost.
deployments.form.idNote: Re-filing an id with different content is refused, not merged.
deployments.form.successMinNote: At 1.00 the deployment can only gate, not rank (HĐ-8.4).
deployments.form.goalToleranceRadNote: Must be ≥ π: arrival heading is not judged (HĐ-6).
deployments.form.clearancePreferenceNote: How much a metre hugging the hard boundary costs against a metre in the open, minus one. At 2.0 a planner takes any detour up to three times as long rather than shave an obstacle. 0 switches the gradient off and plans on distance alone. The only number here nobody can derive — so it is declared once, for every candidate alike.
deployments.form.noiseNote: Belongs to the site and the vehicle, never to the candidate. With σ = 0 and no traffic a deterministic planner replays one episode per seed, so 300 runs carry the information of one — declare one or the other, or say out loud that the deployment is that quiet.
deployments.form.obstacleSpeedEnabled: Declare how fast traffic may close on the robot
deployments.form.obstacleSpeedNote: The speed bound reads the scan the robot has now, which only promises it can stop before an obstacle that is standing. Measured 14-08: a cart driving head-on at 0.2 m/s — slower than walking pace — put the robot through step after step its own criterion called admissible, and it hit; the shipped weights collided too. Declaring this makes the bound cover the ground the obstacle takes while the robot brakes, identically for every candidate. It is checked at load against the traffic declared here, and it needs its own deployment id: HĐ-3.1 does not hash it, so the same deployment with and without it is two experiments.
deployments.form.obstacleSpeedOffNote: Off means undeclared, not zero — this deployment carries no braking guarantee against moving obstacles, and the manifest records that. Zero would be the opposite claim, that nothing at this site moves, and the loader refuses it beside declared traffic.
deployments.form.obstacleSpeedL18Note: Known cost of switching this on: the bound is charged against the nearest LiDAR return of any kind, including shelving that is not going anywhere. In a narrow aisle that throttles the robot to a crawl and the run ends stuck, fifteen metres from the traffic it was meant to brake for (KNOWN_LIMITATIONS L18).
deployments.form.traffic.title: Moving traffic
deployments.form.traffic.note: Traffic belongs to the site, never to a candidate — one obstacle set is what makes two candidates sit the same exam. It is also what gives 300 seeds the information of 300: with no traffic and no noise, a deterministic planner replays one episode per seed.
deployments.form.traffic.name: Name
deployments.form.traffic.nameNote: Two obstacles may not share a name; the server refuses a profile where they do.
deployments.form.traffic.loopNote: At the last waypoint, drive straight back to the first and go round again. The return leg is the dashed line on the map — nobody placed a point on it.
deployments.form.traffic.pingPongNote: At the last waypoint, turn round and retrace the route backwards. With neither box ticked the obstacle drives the route once and parks there for the rest of the episode.
deployments.form.traffic.pathNote: Loop returns along the closing edge; ping-pong retraces the same line. With neither, the obstacle drives the path once and parks at the far end.
deployments.form.traffic.walkSeedNote: Picks which sequence of headings this walker draws. Two walkers sharing a value walk the identical shape, which is rarely what anybody wants.
deployments.form.traffic.heading: Heading (°)
deployments.form.traffic.headingNote: This motion has no end point: the second click sets a direction, and the obstacle travels it until it stops.
deployments.form.traffic.seedTimeOffsetN: Seconds of seed-derived head start on this obstacle's clock. A motion that is a pure function of time — waypoints, back and forth, straight-then-stops — ignores the seed at zero, so every seed replays identical traffic and a multi-seed run reports a variance of zero that is an artefact, not a finding. The server requires a positive value for those, and at least one full period for back-and-forth motion (HĐ-3.3). A random walk draws its headings from the seed already and needs none of this.
deployments.form.traffic.seedTimeOffsetS: One full cycle at the declared speed, which is what makes different seeds meet this obstacle at different points of its route rather than replaying one encounter.
A path driven once has no cycle to derive an offset from, so this one is yours to choose — it still has to be above zero, because the motion itself does not read the seed.
A random walk draws its headings from the seed, so it already differs run to run. Zero is legal here, and the server accepts it.
Fill in the route and the speed and a full cycle can be worked out from them.
deployments.form.traffic.obstacleSeedNot: Mixed into the head-start hash, so two obstacles under one seed do not start their motions in step. Not the same number as the random walk's heading sequence.
deployments.form.traffic.mode.suddenPoin: Click the map to say where {name} comes to rest. Its direction and how long it travels both follow from that point.
deployments.form.traffic.stopModeNote: Two ways to describe one motion. "After a set time" takes a direction and a number of seconds. "At a chosen point" takes the place it ends up, and works the direction and the duration out from it — which is what you mean when you click a spot on the map. Only one of the two is declared: the server refuses a document carrying both, because there would be nothing to decide between them when they disagree.
deployments.form.traffic.stopsAt: Stops at ({x}, {y}) — place it on the map
deployments.form.traffic.parkedFromTheSt: The head start is longer than the {seconds}s this obstacle takes to travel, so about {percent}% of seeds begin after it has already braked — it starts parked at its stopping point and never moves in those episodes. Legal, and sometimes deliberate: the shipped sudden-stop scenario does it, because its cart parks in the robot's lane where blocking the route is the point.
deployments.form.traffic.parkedFix: Use {seconds}s instead — every seed sees it driving
deployments.form.traffic.mode.waypoint: Each click on the map adds a waypoint to {name}.
deployments.form.traffic.mode.periodicSt: Click the map to move where {name} swings from.
deployments.form.traffic.mode.periodicEn: Click the map to move where {name} swings to.
deployments.form.traffic.mode.origin: Click the map to move the point {name} wanders around.
deployments.form.traffic.mode.suddenStar: Click the map to move where {name} sets off from.
deployments.form.traffic.mode.suddenHead: Click the map to aim {name}. Only the direction is kept, not the point.
deployments.form.traffic.flatOnly: Traffic is placed on the flat view. The 2.5D view draws it but does not edit it.
deployments.form.traffic.legendShort: Teal is what you declared; amber is where the server puts it.
deployments.form.traffic.legend: Teal is the traffic as you declared it — routes, points and the obstacle's own size. Amber appears after Preview and is where the server puts each obstacle at that instant; it is a picture, not a control.
deployments.form.undoHint: Ctrl+Z — takes back the last change to this deployment, including a start or goal moved by a stray click on the map.
deployments.form.tabs.label: Deployment settings
deployments.form.validateNote: Runs the same check filing does, without filing anything. It reads the document only, so a clash with an id already on file still surfaces when you file.
deployments.form.previewTimeNote: Which instant of the episode to draw. The traffic is a function of time, so 0 is where every obstacle starts and 40 is where it has got to forty seconds in — useful for asking whether something will be crossing the robot's path when the robot is there.
deployments.form.previewSeedNote: Which run of the many a deployment is measured over. Seeds shift each obstacle's clock by its seed head start and pick a random walk's headings, so the same instant looks different from seed to seed — that difference is the whole reason a comparison runs hundreds of episodes instead of one.
deployments.form.previewInvalid: The server drew this, and it will not run as it stands. These are checks against the map itself, which the document check cannot see:
deployments.form.previewNote: Positions come back from the server, computed by the same function the simulator steps with — a preview that worked them out in the browser would be free to disagree with the episode.
deployments.form.availableRamNote: Total minus the breakdown leaves {left} MB.
decisions.map.heading: heading°
decisions.map.mode.none: Clicking the map does nothing — pick what to place first.
decisions.map.mode.start: Click or drag on the map to move the start.
decisions.map.mode.goal: Click or drag on the map to move the goal.
decisions.map.startHeadingNote: Where the robot faces at t = 0. The simulator starts it in this pose, so a robot pointed away from its goal spends its first second turning — this is part of the mission, not a drawing detail.
decisions.map.goalHeadingNote: Stored and drawn, but never judged: this platform has no final-orientation controller, so every deployment must declare goal_tolerance_rad ≥ π and arrival is decided on position alone (HĐ-6). Changing this changes no verdict.
decisions.map.note: A different map is a different world, so this files a NEW deployment rather than editing the chosen one: episode_context_id does not hash the map (HĐ-3.1), and reusing the id would let episodes from two worlds collide on one hash. Start and goal are required, and the server checks them against the map before storing — a goal inside a shelf gives every candidate 0% success, and the comparison would then report a tie on a question none of them was asked.
deployments.form.localizationDriftNote: How wrong the robot's idea of its own pose gets. Reaches Observation, never the collision test.
deployments.form.lidarDropoutNote: A dropped return reads to a costmap as free space — this is how a robot drives into glass.
deployments.form.odometryBiasNote: Drawn once per episode and held, so it accumulates instead of averaging out like wheel slip.

candidates.title: Candidates
candidates.subtitle: A candidate is one stack plus one controller configuration, identified by the hash of that pair (HĐ-1.3).
candidates.register.title: Register a candidate
candidates.register.signedOut: Sign in to register a candidate.
candidates.register.note: There is no id field: HĐ-1.3 makes candidate_id a hash over the stack, its parameters and its code version, so the server computes it. A caller-supplied id would let two different configurations share an identity that every trace, pairing and ΔU keys on.
candidates.registered.title: Registered candidates
candidates.registered.silenceNote: Not the same as zero. The objectives layer charges an undeclared candidate for the silence rather than substituting nothing, so it cannot be scored on cheapest-to-own.
candidates.registered.idNote: The id is the identity. Two candidates differing only in a sampling parameter are two candidates, and every trace file is named after this hash.
candidates.registered.empty.title: No candidate registered yet
candidates.registered.empty.body: A comparison can still name a stack and a configuration directly; registering one first is how it gets an id you can quote.
candidates.stacks.title: Stacks in the registry
candidates.stacks.referenceNote: Exists to validate the pipeline and must never support a conclusion, so it is not offered when choosing a candidate.
candidates.stacks.stochasticNote: This planner draws random samples, so it needs more seeds to say anything. A report that hid this would invite comparing one lucky tree against A*.
candidates.configs.title: Controller configurations
candidates.configs.name: Name
candidates.configs.note: The numbers, not just the names: dwa_coarse samples 7×15 where dwa_default samples 20×40. That difference is the whole reason a sampling choice is a candidate rather than a constant inside whichever script ran.
candidates.pick.noConfigs: No named configuration for this controller yet.
decisions.tally.note: Counts, not a ranking. A recommendation is scoped to one deployment and says nothing about any other map, mission or robot (HĐ-1.4) — so decision utility appears only once this list is filtered to a single deployment.
decisions.workspaceSubtitle: Compare two candidates on the same deployment, mission, seeds and evaluation conditions.
decisions.launch.needMap: Complete the custom map before running.
bench.title: Test bench
bench.subtitle: Run one episode to inspect motion, verify configuration and catch issues before benchmarking.
bench.noticeSummary: Episodes here are not benchmark results and do not create traces for Decision Cards.
bench.setupSubtitle: Choose the conditions, candidate and seed for a reproducible run.
bench.help.mission: The selected start, goal and scenario.
bench.help.seed: The same seed reproduces the same situation.
bench.help.global: The algorithm that creates the global path.
bench.help.local: The controller that avoids obstacles and follows the path.
bench.disabled.candidate: Choose a global planner, local controller and configuration.
bench.notEvidence: Nothing here is a measurement. The conditions are the deployment's own, so what you watch is what a comparison will run — but no trace is written, so no gate, metric or Decision Card can see this episode (HĐ-5).
bench.seedNote: The same seed is the same episode, down to the obstacle trajectories and the noise draws — so you can watch one again, slower.
bench.signedOut: Sign in to run an episode.
bench.conditionsNote: Fixed conditions taken from the deployment and kept unchanged for this episode.
bench.conditionsLockedHint: To change these conditions, edit or create another deployment.
bench.conditionsSummary: Start {start} → Goal {goal} · Robot {radius} · Replan {replanning} · {traffic} dynamic obstacles
bench.contextIdNote: — the real HĐ-3.1 hash, so this is the same episode a comparison would run.
bench.selectDeployment: Pick a deployment and a candidate, then run one episode.
bench.metricsNote: Read off this run, not off a trace — the right numbers for “did that look sane” and the wrong ones for any claim.
bench.nextNote: Once one episode looks right, a comparison runs the same conditions across every candidate and enough seeds to say something.
bench.empty.title: No deployments yet
bench.empty.body: The test bench runs an episode of a deployment, so there has to be one first.
deployments.form.vehicleNote: Choosing a vehicle fills the limits below; they stay editable, and the deployment stores the numbers rather than a reference — so a later edit to the vehicle cannot change what an already-measured run described (HĐ-13). Control period is not filled: it is this site's requirement, not the robot's property.
deployments.form.vehicleUndeclared: This vehicle never declared its accelerations, so those two fields were left as they were. Absent is not zero — fill them from the datasheet rather than letting a leftover number be measured as fact.
decisions.gates.observationUnknownNote: The registry has no entry for this stack, so nobody wrote down what it was given. It cannot be shown to have run on the same inputs as the others.
decisions.gates.mixedObservation: These candidates were shown different things ({classes}). A stack reading the static map and one reading only its LiDAR are answering different questions, so most of the gap between their numbers is the gap between their inputs — ΔU here measures the privilege as much as the planner. Read the ranking accordingly, or re-run with candidates that saw the same world.
dashboard.stats.rankedHint: Most runs do not — a gate table is still a result
dashboard.empty.decisions.title: No comparisons yet
dashboard.empty.decisions.body: A comparison weighs candidates on one deployment and, when two of them clear the gates, produces a Decision Card.
mapView.editInFlat: Switch to top-down to place or paint — the raised view has no inverse projection, so a click cannot name a cell.
trace.flatHasClearance: The top-down view colours the path by clearance; this one does not.
trace.missing: No trace is available for this candidate.
trace.loadError: This candidate's trace could not be loaded.
trace.tip.result: The final episode verdict recorded by the backend.
trace.tip.time: Travel time recorded for this episode.
trace.tip.clearance: Minimum robot-surface clearance recorded for this episode.
trace.tip.latency: P99 planner latency recorded for this episode.
trace.tip.collision: Collision count recorded for this episode.
trace.tip.replan: Replans recorded for this episode; a dash means not reported.
trace.legend.title: Map legend
deployments.delete.blocked: This deployment has {runs} stored run(s), {approved} of them approved. Every run is a statement about this deployment — without it they describe nothing.
deployments.delete.approvedWarning: An approved run is a configuration somebody signed off. Deleting it removes that record and its review trail (HĐ-14).
deployments.delete.approvedBlocked: This deployment has {approved} approved run(s). An approved run is a configuration somebody signed off, together with the record of who signed it (HĐ-14), so no confirmation here can delete it. Withdraw the approval on the run first — it stays in the journal beside the withdrawal.
decisions.withdraw.note: Returns this run to undecided. The approval is not erased — it stays in the journal below, with the withdrawal beside it (HĐ-14).
decisions.gates.replanNote: How many times this candidate replanned across every episode. Evidence, not a score — replanning already costs time and latency, and both are charged. There is no replan budget: the price is that every replan records its own control step, so habitual replanning walks into G4 on its own.
deployments.form.replanningEnabled: Let candidates replan when the robot gets stuck
deployments.form.replanningNote: Same trigger and no budget, for every candidate alike: replan as often as it takes, bounded by the episode timeout. Each replan is charged to the control step it delayed, so p99 latency and travel time already price it — a stack that needs more replans pays more without a penalty term. Switching this on is a different experiment from the same deployment with it off, so it needs its own deployment id (HĐ-3.1 does not hash it).
deployments.form.recoveryNote: When replanning finds no route, the robot may act to change its situation instead of asking the same question again: wait, back up, turn towards the path, and — last — discard what it has sensed. Each rung costs simulation time and distance, so it is paid for in the metrics rather than by a penalty term.
deployments.form.recoveryEscalationNote: How far up the ladder wait / back up / turn / forget the robot may climb. 3 allows everything except discarding what it saw.
deployments.form.recoveryForgets: Times it may forget what it sensed
deployments.form.recoveryForgetsNote: The last rung replans on the static map alone, throwing away every LiDAR return. It changes belief rather than the world, so it is capped and counted: a second one is forgetting twice.
bench.replanningOn: on — unlimited, each replan charged to the step it delays
bench.replanningOff: off — the robot must get through with the local controller alone
deployments.form.replanningTraffic: This scenario has {n} moving obstacle(s). With replanning off, a candidate blocked by one has only its local controller to get around it — which is a legitimate experiment, but decide it rather than inherit it.
mapView.keepOut: The faint ring is the margin the global planner will not route through — the robot's radius plus one cell diagonal. It is not a collision boundary: the local controller drives inside it whenever it squeezes past something.
decisions.preview.empty: Choose a deployment to review the map and conditions used for this comparison.
decisions.preview.title: Selected deployment
decisions.preview.readonlyTip: These conditions were fixed in Deployment. Edit or create another deployment to change them.
decisions.preview.sharedNotice: Candidate A and Candidate B will run on the same map, mission, robot, seed, and conditions shown here.
decisions.preview.mapLabel: Read-only map for the selected deployment
decisions.preview.mapUnavailable: This deployment's map could not be loaded.
trace.sync.loading: Aligning both runs along the route…
trace.sync.error: Could not align these two runs.
trace.sync.quality.degraded_candidate_pa: No planned route recorded — projected onto a driven path
trace.sync.quality.degraded_straight_lin: No planned route recorded — projected onto start→goal
trace.exemplar.title: Chosen for you
trace.exemplar.why.typical: ΔU closest to the median — calibrate on this one.
trace.exemplar.why.strongest_for_winner: Where candidate A won hardest. Shown together with B's best, never alone.
trace.exemplar.why.safety_critical: Worst safety outcome across both candidates, whatever the utility says.
explain.title: Why this result
explain.headline.nearEquivalent: The two are near-equivalent; here is what separates them.
explain.headline.noSurvivors: No recommendation: fewer than two candidates cleared the gates.
explain.headline.gateOnly: No recommendation: this deployment cannot rank anybody.
explain.headline.interrupted: Interrupted run — what it did measure.
explain.headline.interruptedBeforeRankin: Interrupted before any comparison was made.
explain.caveat.scope: Holds under the simulated scenario distribution declared for this deployment.
explain.caveat.insideTheNoise: The interval of ΔU covers zero: the ranking did not decide this.
explain.caveat.tieBreak: The declared tie-break ladder chose the recommendation.
explain.caveat.fewerEpisodes: Fewer episodes than requested; every number here rests on that smaller sample.
explain.caveat.noComparisonYet: This run stopped before a paired comparison existed, so there is no ΔU to explain.
explain.caveat.registerABetterCandidate: The fix is a better candidate — never a softer deployment.
explain.caveat.deploymentCannotRank: Use a deployment whose threshold leaves room above it; no candidate changes this.
evidence.title: Evidence behind this run
evidence.unavailable: This run was scored before the explanation layer existed, so it has no evidence packet. Re-run the comparison to get one.
evidence.noComparison: This run ranked nobody, so there is no pair to decompose. What follows is what was seen while the candidates ran.
evidence.waterfall.lede: Weighted utility difference over the shared episodes:
evidence.waterfall.median: Median ΔU, not decomposed — the bars sum through the mean only
evidence.sightings.title: What the detectors saw
evidence.sightings.none: No episode traces were available, so no detector ran.
evidence.sightings.clean: The detectors ran and found nothing. That is the finding.
evidence.lattice.title: What the contrast supports
evidence.gaps.title: What this platform cannot know yet
evidence.omissions.title: What could not be built, and why
evidence.comparisonWithheld: The panel plan withholds a comparison for this outcome.
running.title: Who is doing better, right now
running.none: No running comparison for this episode — this deployment's objective anchors could not be resolved, and the composite is the platform's own curves rather than a stand-in for them.
running.before: Neither run has reached the first rung of the ladder yet.
running.clock.progress: At the same point of the route
running.clock.progress.hint: How the same stretch of task was done. Read here because both runs have covered the same ground.
running.clock.time.hint: Position in the task, not quality of it. At one instant the two robots are in different places, so these say who is further on — nothing about the part they have not reached.
running.metric.exposure_s: Time spent inside the warning distance
running.metric.compute_budget: Planner latency p99, against the control period
running.composite.title: Safety-versus-efficiency, over the part that has happened
running.composite.partial: Not ΔU. Two of four objectives — reaching the goal has no value halfway through — and efficiency is measured against the replay's reference line, not L_ref. The episode's real utility is on the card.
running.rulerArtefact: This run recorded no plan, so this candidate's own path became the reference line — its efficiency is 1.00 by construction, not by merit.
trace.tip.lastEvent: The final HĐ-5 event the trace recorded. Beside Result, which is the gate's reading of the same episode — the two are only usually the same word.
trace.metricsView.hint: This replay swaps its live readings for the episode's result when it runs out. This asks for that result now, for this candidate only.
trace.latencyChart.title: Planner latency (ms)
trace.latencyChart.alt: Planner latency over the episode, against the deployment's control period.
trace.latencyChart.noPlanning: The planner did not run during this episode, so there is no latency to plot.
decisions.gates.blocks.G1: Blocks a planner that too often finds no route at all: no_path_rate above the deployment's no_path_rate_max. Kept apart from G3 because failing to find a route and having a route not survive traffic are different jobs, fixed on different layers.
decisions.gates.blocks.G2: Blocks any collision at all — and a clean record on too few *distinct* runs to mean anything. Zero collisions in 10 runs is consistent with a 26% collision rate, so the deployment's accepted risk fixes N_min rather than the run size deciding what may be claimed (HĐ-7.1).
decisions.gates.blocks.G3: Blocks too many episodes that never reached the goal, however they failed: success_rate below the deployment's success_rate_min.
decisions.gates.blocks.G4: Blocks a planner that misses control deadlines: p99 latency above one control period, pooled over every control step of the evaluation set. Measured on the benchmark host — there is no conversion factor to the target board, and inventing one is banned (HĐ-7.2).
decisions.gates.blocks.G5: Blocks a stack that would not fit the board's navigation RAM budget. The estimate is data-structure counts at the target implementation's byte sizes, never the Python process's RSS. Passing is an elimination test that came out negative, not a certificate of fit (HĐ-7.3).
decisions.gates.blocks.G6: Blocks a candidate that needs an observation this deployment does not provide. Decided before a single episode runs, so a candidate can be excluded without ever being driven.
decisions.env.unpinned: Measured on all {cores} cores, unpinned: G4 reads latency by the wall clock, so every other load on the machine goes straight into the number. The same candidate measured {unpinned} ms unpinned and {pinned} ms pinned to 2 cores
decisions.compare.title: How they ended up
decisions.compare.note: The numbers the sweep concluded on, read across each row. Every value the gates already produced is taken from the gate that decided on it, so nothing here can disagree with a verdict above. Decision utility is not a row: the card carries it for the recommended candidate only, and a mean taken here would be a second scoring path.
decisions.compare.worstClearance: Worst clearance in the whole run
decisions.compare.memory: Memory estimate on the target board
decisions.compare.why.successRate: The share of episodes that reached the goal, however the rest failed. G3 judges this against the deployment's success_rate_min.
decisions.compare.why.collisions: Taken from G2's own count. One collision ends the gate, so this is a zero-or-eliminated column rather than a scale.
decisions.compare.why.collisionBound: What the clean record actually supports. Zero collisions in 10 distinct runs is consistent with a 26% collision rate; the bound is 3/N under the simulated scenario distribution, so a lower number here means a larger evidence base, not a safer robot.
decisions.compare.why.noPathRate: How often the global planner returned nothing at all. G1 keeps this apart from a general failure rate because not finding a route and having a route not survive traffic are fixed on different layers.
decisions.compare.why.worstClearance: The closest the robot ever came to anything, across every episode. A run whose typical clearance is comfortable can still hold one near miss, and an average would hide it.
decisions.compare.why.medianTravel: How long a typical episode took. The median rather than the mean: one timeout parked at the deployment's cap drags a mean by tens of seconds, and the number then describes the cap rather than the stack.
decisions.compare.why.p99: The 99th percentile over every control step of the evaluation set, pooled. G4 judges it against one control period and measures on the benchmark host — there is no conversion factor to the target board.
decisions.compare.why.memory: G5's estimate from data-structure counts at the target implementation's byte sizes, never the Python process's RSS. Under budget is an elimination test that came out negative, not a certificate of fit.
decisions.compare.why.distinctEpisodes: How many of the episodes were actually different from each other. A deterministic stack on traffic that never crosses its route produces the same episode once per seed, and a hundred copies bound a risk exactly as well as one does.
decisions.compare.why.replans: Evidence, not a score — which is why no candidate is marked ahead on this row. Replanning already costs travel time and latency, and both are charged; there is no separate replan budget to come in under.
conclusion.title: Which stack to use
conclusion.note: The platform's own decision utility, shown out of 100. Candidates that cleared every gate are ranked above the line and may be recommended; the rest are marked too, because on this deployment nobody clears everything yet — but their marks do not compare across the line. A gate failure can leave no trace in the number: collisions are excluded from U_S by contract so that they cannot be traded against speed, and no objective reflects a missing observation channel.
conclusion.eligible.hint: Ranked, and eligible to be recommended. The mark ranks within this group.
conclusion.blocked.hint: Marked so this deployment has something to read while no stack clears everything, but never ranked against the group above: a failure that the utility cannot see would let the wrong candidate look best.
conclusion.g2.sample: G2: too few distinct episodes, no collision observed
conclusion.markCannotSee.hint: Collisions are excluded from U_S on purpose (HĐ-6): letting them lower a score would imply they can be traded against speed. No objective reflects a missing observation channel either. So for these failures the mark is unchanged by the thing that disqualified the candidate.
conclusion.headline.nearEquivalent: The field could not be separated: the platform reports these as near-equivalent, which is a result rather than a missing answer.
conclusion.headline.noCard: No recommendation: fewer than two candidates cleared every gate, so ΔU does not exist for this run.
conclusion.headline.bestSoFar: {stack} carries the highest mark, which is not the same as being recommended.
conclusion.objective.U_R: Reaching the goal — the share of episodes that arrived.
conclusion.objective.U_S: Safety, from near-miss rate and worst clearance. Collisions are deliberately absent: they live at gate G2 and nowhere else (HĐ-6).
conclusion.objective.U_E: Efficiency — path and time against the route the map allows.
conclusion.objective.U_C: Cost — planner latency, memory estimate and CPU time.
